argument: I tried to move the date. The 2020 interim analysis is excluded by the criterion. MAPS's release of 2021-05-03 reports a significant reduction on the primary PTSD-severity measure versus placebo with therapy (p<0.0001); Nature Medicine published the paper on 2021-05-10; ClinicalTrials.gov results were first submitted 2021-08-18 and posted 2021-09-16. I found no earlier public report: MAPS's own 2021-05-21 summary says the results were announced May 3 and published May 10. The release came from MAPS, the parent of sponsor MAPS PBC, which the criterion accepts as the sponsor's topline release. Occurred on 2021-05-03 stands.

The recorded resolution counts the FTC stipulation over data and cancellation practices as a settlement over Cerebral's 'business practices'. Under the same reading an earlier qualifying settlement exists. On 2023-12-28 the New York Attorney General announced an agreement under which Cerebral, Inc. pays $200,000 in penalties and $540,162 in restitution to 16,552 New Yorkers for a burdensome cancellation process, charges after cancellation and manipulated online reviews. A state attorney general is a named enforcement agency, and the criterion fixes an agency settlement's date by the agency press release. I found no earlier qualifying action: the N.D. Iowa qui tam was dismissed without judgment, and the DOJ and FTC matters closed later. The first-true date moves from 2024-04-15 to 2023-12-28; the state is unchanged.

PubMed shows no qualifying multi-daily theta-burst RCT in depression from 2022-07-12 to 2024-07-10: Wilkening 2022 and Li 2023 missed their primary endpoints; Kong 2023 was a non-inferiority trial of V1 versus DLPFC with no sham arm; Huang 2024, Zhang 2024 and Mallik 2022 were not significant. So Sheline et al. (JAMA Psychiatry online 2024-07-10; 10 sessions a day for 5 days; MADRS -14.75 versus sham, P<.001) is the first positive RCT, but its population is treatment-refractory bipolar depression. The criterion says "a depressive disorder"; DSM-5 files bipolar disorders in a separate chapter, while the proposition says "for depression" and the registered conditions include treatment-resistant depression. If bipolar depression is excluded, the next candidate is Ramos et al. (online 2025-03-05; TRD; 3 sessions a day for 15 weekdays), outside the "about five days" reading. The readings differ by eight months; the criterion does not settle it.

I looked for an earlier Magnus announcement of commercial availability or of a first commercial patient. The Business Wire list of Magnus releases and the company's own release index show nothing between the 2023-10-23 CPT-code release, which only anticipates hospital claims once the codes take effect on 2024-07-01, and the 2024-04-30 'Commercial Launch' release that names the first customer sites. CMS's FY 2024 IPPS final rule records the applicant telling CMS that SAINT 'will be commercially available on April 15, 2024', and UAMS's 'first in the nation to offer' release is dated 2024-06-11; neither is a Magnus press release, the only source the criterion accepts. FDA clearance (2022-09-06) and the OLO trial (2023-07-20) are excluded. Occurred on 2024-04-30 stands.

The 2023-01-05 release (PR Newswire and mapsbcorp.com) says MAPP2 'met both the primary endpoint as measured by the change from baseline in CAPS-5 and the key secondary endpoint', but it gives no p-value and never says 'statistically significant'; the parent MAPS post of the same day gives no efficacy statistic at all. One could push the date to the Nature Medicine paper (2023-09-14, P<0.001) or the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting (2023-10-11). I do not: a sponsor's statement that a trial 'met' its prespecified primary endpoint is the standard report that the prespecified test reached significance, the publication confirmed it, and the criterion accepts significance 'as reported by the sponsor'. No earlier disclosure exists; the 2022-11-17 completion release only promised topline results in Q1 2023. Occurred on 2023-01-05 stands.

The recorded date relies on NCT05163496 being 'registered as Phase 3'. Its ClinicalTrials.gov version history shows otherwise: the versions of 2021-12-06, 2021-12-17 and 2022-07-13 list Phase 1/Phase 2, and the July 2022 version already carries the actual start date 2022-03-03; the Phase 3 label first appears in the 2023-05-17 version, fourteen months after the start. So on 2022-03-03 a trial registered as Phase 1/2 started, and no psilocybin trial registered as Phase 3 had started. The first psilocybin trial registered as Phase 3 when it started is COMPASS's COMP005 (NCT05624268), posted 2022-11-22 as Phase 3 with actual start 2023-01-24; no sponsor first-patient release predates that, and the ClinicalTrials.gov Phase 3 search shows no other candidate before it. The first-true date moves to 2023-01-24; the state is unchanged.

I argued that the 2023 proposal was never revised, withdrawn or replaced: no withdrawal notice exists, and the 2025-01-17 NPRM never uses the words withdraw, supersede or replace. The text of 90 FR 6541 defeats this. It is issued under the same RIN 1117-AB40 and docket DEA-407; it says DEA 'reevaluated its approach and determined that the best course of action was to proceed with the promulgation of a Special Registration rule', which 'no longer contains an in-person medical examination requirement for certain substances' nor the 30-day supply limit; and its Regulatory Alternatives section lists 'finalizing the proposed March 2023 General Telemedicine NPRM' as a rejected alternative. That is a new proposal that supersedes the 2023 one. The same-day VA final rule (90 FR 6523; RIN 1117-AB40; docket DEA-2023-0029) partially finalizes the rulemaking on different terms, also on 2025-01-17. Nothing earlier in the docket qualifies. Occurred on 2025-01-17 stands.

The criterion fixes the date at the DEA announcement date when it is earlier than Federal Register publication. The resolver used DEA's press release of 2023-05-09 on the temporary rule (filed 2023-05-09, published 2023-05-10, effective 2023-05-11). DEA made an earlier public announcement: the Administrator's statement of 2023-05-03 (dea.gov, dated in its URL and quoted by K&L Gates and trade press; dea.gov refuses automated fetches) said DEA had received a record 38,000 comments and 'we have decided to extend the current flexibilities while we work to find a way forward'. Read as the DEA announcement of the extension, the first-true date is 2023-05-03. Read strictly, the statement announced a decision but no rule or order, and the rule was first announced on 2023-05-09. The criterion does not say which announcement counts. The state is unaffected; the date needs a ruling.

I tried to move the date to DEA's announcement of 2023-10-06 ('DEA and HHS Extend Telemedicine Flexibilities through 2024') or to the public-inspection posting. Unlike E-0014, this criterion names only the Federal Register publication date. The Federal Register API gives publication_date 2023-10-10 for 88 FR 69879 (document 2023-22406, docket DEA-407), a temporary rule that extends the full flexibilities through 2024-12-31, beyond the 2023-11-11 end date and the 2024-11-11 grace period set by the first extension of 2023-05-10. It is a temporary rule, not a permanent replacement. The third (2024-11-19) and fourth (2025-12-31) extensions do not change the first-true date. Occurred on 2023-10-10 stands.

I tested whether the date should be the publication date (2023-08-28) or the display date (2023-08-01) rather than the effective date, and whether the approval was final. The FY 2024 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule (88 FR 58640) states 'we are finalizing that the maximum new technology add-on payment for a case involving the use of the SAINT Neuromodulation System is $12,675.00 for FY 2024', with cases identified by ICD-10-PCS X0Z0X18, and 'DATES: This final rule is effective October 1, 2023.' The criterion names the effective date, so 2023-10-01 is correct. No earlier IPPS rule approved an NTAP for SAINT; FDA clearance came 2022-09-06, after the FY 2023 application cycle. The rule also records the applicant's statement that SAINT would be commercially available on 2024-04-15, which bears on the newness period, not on approval. Occurred on 2023-10-01 stands.

Attacked the date both ways. Earlier: Magnus's 2024-04-30 launch release names UAMS and MUSC Health as 'first customer sites' and quotes UAMS as 'first site in the nation to offer' SAINT, but the teams 'will implement' it and no patient availability or treated patient is stated: an agreement to install, which the criterion excludes. MUSC in fact treated patients first: its article of 2024-08-09 (musc.edu) says MUSC was 'the first hospital system in the country to actually perform the SAINT method for patients in May' 2024; the Post and Courier (2024-08-19) agrees. But the criterion keys on the announcement date, and MUSC's first public announcement came 2024-08-09, after the UAMS release of 2024-06-11, which states SAINT 'can only be provided to patients who are being treated as inpatients'. No hospital or Magnus announcement of patient availability between 2024-04-30 and 2024-06-11 was found. 2024-06-11 stands; UAMS's 'first' claim is wrong in fact but not in date.

Verified K260402 (Wave Neuroscience MeRT, new product code SIG, 21 CFR 882.5802, decision 2026-06-03, PTSD) in the FDA 510(k) database and openFDA. openFDA lists 24 OBP (MDD) and 2 QCI (OCD) clearances from 2024-01-05 to 2026-09-13, no new QMD or OKP entries, and SIG as the only new TMS product code. Population and protocol clearances (NeuroStar adolescents K231926 2024-03-22; Magstim K243869; MagVenture K251119; BrainsWay K251391; Nexstim K252358) are excluded by the criterion text. Magstim's 2025-07-09 'pain' clearance is peripheral nerve stimulation held since K992911 (2000), not a new TMS condition. So under the criterion as written 2026-06-03 is right. But reading 5 says 'a new patient population for a listed disorder counts as a new indication', which makes K231926 (2024-03-22) the first-true date, 26 months earlier and possibly inside deadlines the criterion text resolves FALSE. Criterion and readings contradict each other; a human must pick which governs.

Looked for an earlier or later first report. The GlobeNewswire release is dated 2025-07-01 06:00 ET (also an 8-K exhibit that day) and reports the primary endpoint of the quadruple-masked, dose-finding core stage of Phase 2b NCT05870540: MADRS change at Day 29, 12 mg vs 0.3 mg, -11.1 vs -5.8 points, p=0.0038, n=193. Beckley's Phase 2a open-label TRD data (2024) and the enrollment-complete release carry no primary endpoint; the open-label extension topline (2025-11-10) came later; no conference abstract, interim or pooled analysis preceded 2025-07-01; the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting (2026-09-10) is later. The sponsor is Beckley Psytech with parent atai, as the criterion allows. 2025-07-01 stands.

Argued that Lykos's 2024-08-09 disclosure names only non-safety grounds (durability, expectancy bias, psychotherapy) and that a request for a new trial is not a request for safety data. It fails: the release (PR Newswire, 2024-08-09 17:27 ET) says the FDA 'requested that Lykos conduct an additional Phase 3 trial to further study the safety and efficacy of midomafetamine', a request for additional safety data with other deficiencies, so the FALSE branch ('only deficiencies that do not concern safety data') does not apply. The letter, signed 2024-08-08 14:39 and published by FDA on 2025-09-04, confirms it: the NDA did not 'establish the safety', unreported adverse events raise 'substantial concerns about the reliability of the safety data', Phase 3 laboratory data were missing, and FDA asked for a new trial to 'adequately characterize the safety'. The letter date is earlier, but the criterion keys on the sponsor's disclosure, and FDA said nothing publicly before 2025. 2024-08-09 stands.

The resolver flagged that state-court patient suits were not searched. One exists: Dustin Fogt v. Options Behavioral Health System and Acadia Healthcare Company Inc., Marion Superior Court No. 49D13-2409-CT-044449, filed 2024-09-30 (Mirror Indy, 2024-10-03: 'a Sept. 30 lawsuit'; The Indiana Lawyer, 2024-12-04, confirms it). He alleges he was held three days beyond his involuntary hold, was threatened with longer detention if he pressed charges, and that Options held patients 'based not on treatment decisions, but upon the maximum amount the center could bill' insurance: the NYT conduct, against Acadia and a subsidiary, after 2024-09-04 and 16 days before Kachrodia. Nothing earlier surfaced: Dufour's 2024-09-11 filing was a proposed malpractice complaint with the Indiana Department of Insurance, not a court docket; Jenkins (W.D. Tenn., 2024-09-18) is an employment case; the DOJ settlement of 2024-09-26 resolved qui tam suits filed in 2017. First-true date: 2024-09-30.

Attacked the fit: the sponsor labels the trial an 'exploratory, double-blind, placebo-controlled, first-in-patient Phase 2a study' with a safety and tolerability primary endpoint, while the criterion asks for 'the Phase 2 trial' and its 'primary-endpoint result'. The attack fails: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06693609 lists the study as Phase 2 and it is the only Phase 2 trial of EMP-01 in social anxiety disorder; the release (GlobeNewswire, 2026-02-26 07:00 ET) reports the primary endpoint (safety and tolerability through Day 43, met) and the LSAS efficacy result (placebo-adjusted -11.85 points, Hedges' g 0.45, p=0.036 one-tailed; 71 enrolled, 70 dosed, 69 completed) in the sponsor's own topline release, which the criterion names as the primary source. Web search finds no earlier disclosure of these results; the 'additional Phase 2a results' release came later. Direction is stored, not required. 2026-02-26 stands.

Attacked the date. Earlier: PubMed (E-utilities) shows no journal publication of NCT04593875, and the only pallidal tFUS trial paper in Parkinson's disease (Lin, Mov Disord, epub 2025-10-23) used a Taiwanese device, not Brainsonix. Of 26 tFUS papers dated 2026-01-01 to 2026-02-04, none is a peer-reviewed patient trial of a Brainsonix device: Schachtner (Front Psychiatry, 2026-01-20) used an Openwater device, Subramaniam (medRxiv, 2026-01-13) is a preprint, the coupling-pad paper is preclinical. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 22 Brainsonix or BX Pulsar studies and only NCT04593875 has results posted after 2026-01-01 (first posted 2026-02-04; UCLA; BX Pulsar 1002; 31 Parkinson's patients; randomized sham-controlled crossover; UPDRS-III, finger tapping and pegboard primary outcomes reported). Later: the Brainsonix news page has no topline release; its 2026 items relay older or healthy-volunteer papers. No prior publication or abstract made the results public before 2026. 2026-02-04 stands.

An earlier 2026 complaint fits the criterion as applied at least as well as H.N.: M.M. v. Aetna Life Insurance Co., Bank of America Corp., its Corporate Benefits Committee and its Group Benefits Program, W.D.N.C. No. 3:26-cv-00219, filed 2026-03-19. It names the employer as sponsor of a self-funded plan and the plan committee as administrator, pleads that they 'are fiduciaries of the Plan' (para 13) and 'breached their fiduciary duties' (para 66), and its Second Cause of Action, 'Violation of the MHPAEA (29 U.S.C. 1132(a)(3))', says 'these MHPAEA violations by Defendants are breaches of fiduciary duty' (para 78). H.N. (2026-03-26) instead concedes 'Marsh played no role in the decision' (para 3). Both are single-family benefit suits, not the Schlichter-style class actions in the readings; under that reading neither counts (RECAP shows no such 2026 suit). Under the criterion as written the first-true date moves to 2026-03-19, if in window; an earlier 2026 filing may exist outside RECAP.

Checked for an earlier or later first report. Definium's Q2 2026 release (2026-08-06) says only that Voyage enrollment was complete (214 randomized) and that 'topline data anticipated the week of August 10, 2026', with no result. The topline release (ir.definiumtx.com and Business Wire, 2026-08-12 07:00 ET) reports the primary endpoint: HAM-A change at week 12, -11.6 (DT120 ODT 100 ug) vs -6.2 (placebo), difference -5.4, p<0.0001, and calls it the Company's second Phase 3 readout after Emerge (MDD, June), a different trial. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06741228 (Definium Therapeutics US; primary completion 2026-07-15; last update 2026-09-02) has no results posted, and no peer-reviewed publication or conference abstract with the primary estimate predates the release; Panorama (September) is a different trial. 2026-08-12 stands.

Argued the second qualifying case is not 2026-06-18. Checked whether either docket fails the criterion and whether an earlier second case exists. Both dockets hold. E.D. Pa.: DiRenzo, Matozzo and PA Norris were indicted for conspiracy to unlawfully distribute Schedule II drugs through a voicemail refill line, a clinic prescriber and its principals, announced 2026-06-23 in the national takedown. S.D. Tex.: Crowder, Durham and pharmacist Onuaguluchi were indicted over two Houston pill-mill clinics and a Conroe pharmacy, 3.4 million pills; distinct docket, different companies. Neither is a Done Global superseding indictment. I found no dated earlier 2026 filing that moves the second-case date back; searches returned 2024-2025 cases, pleas and convictions in existing dockets. Residual risk: the sweep is not exhaustive, and the statement date is not shown, so 'filed after the statement date' stays unverified.

Argued the date is wrong or the trial does not qualify. Three attacks failed. (1) Device: the PMC full text names the Monarch TNS System (NeuroSigma), the cleared device. (2) Size and design: ATTENS randomized 150 (75/75) against 62 in McGough 2019 (NCT02155608), the trial behind the April 2019 FDA clearance, and is described as a confirmatory replication, so it meets 'larger' and 'designed to test'. (3) Date: the window edge is tight, because the criterion needs a date after 2026-01-15 and the paper is Epub 2026-01-16. The Nature Medicine DOI carries a 2025 stem (s41591-025-04075-x), so I checked for an earlier online date; PubMed, PMC and Nature all give 16 January 2026, print Feb 2026;32(2):582-590. Nothing qualifying falls in the one-day gap, and UCLA NCT05374187 (n=218) has posted no results. The null primary result does not matter, because any direction counts.

Attacked the date. The gap the resolver left open breaks it. Nasdaq added Atai Beckley N.V. (ATAI) to the Nasdaq Biotechnology Index in the December 2025 annual reconstitution, effective before the open on 2025-12-22; the company confirmed this on 2025-12-23, and a peer addition release dated 2025-12-16 shows Nasdaq had announced the reconstitution by then. The NBI is a named qualifying index, so the first qualifying announcement is Nasdaq's December 2025 notice, about five months before the Russell 3000 preliminary list of 2026-05-22. The Russell facts themselves stand: ATAI is on the 2026-05-22 preliminary list and the final list, effective 2026-06-29. Which date is first-true turns on the statement date, which I cannot see. If the statement predates the December 2025 announcement, the date moves to that notice; if it postdates it, ATAI was already an NBI constituent, NBI is excluded and 2026-05-22 stands.

Attacked the 2023-02-03 date. The Premera policy history in the 2026-08-01 PDF does support it: the 11/01/22 entry says changes effective Feb. 3, 2023 made standard and deep TMS medically necessary for OCD and added criteria for accelerated intensive TMS. But the 2023 text gated accelerated TMS on hardship. The 05/01/23 entry adds hardship examples, and the 01/01/26 entry (approved 2025-12-09) says coverage was expanded 'by removing the hardship requirement'. So in 2023 Premera allowed a compressed schedule for a conventional course, not an accelerated protocol; SNT/SAINT was, and still is, investigational, and SWIFT was named medically necessary only on 2026-08-01. BrainsWay's 2026-01-07 release calls the January 2026 Premera policy the first coverage policy for accelerated deep TMS, which contradicts a 2023 first-true date. Candidate alternative: 2026-01-01. The sources conflict on what counts as a protocol.

Attacked the criterion and the 2024-07-01 date. The IBX facts hold: the provider notice revises 07.03.22f and MA07.035e to make accelerated theta burst stimulation (SAINT, 10 daily sessions over five days) medically necessary, retroactively effective 2024-07-01, with the final policy issued 2024-12-02. Two problems. First, 2024-07-01 is a retroactive effective date; no policy was published on that day, and the notice carries no publication date in the evidence, so 'the effective date of a published medical policy' is strained. Second, and larger, the criterion resolves TRUE almost two years before the 2026-05-16 statement it scores. The forecaster said 'more to come' after listing seven plans; a policy already in force in 2024 shows the list was incomplete, not that the forecast came true. The resolver also concedes that earlier policies from other plans were not ruled out, so 2024-07-01 is not established as first-true.

Case for an earlier date: NPR, MJBizDaily and law-firm posts all report that DEA 'approved' Scottsdale Research Institute and Biopharmaceutical Research Company in May 2021, and DEA's own 2021-05-14 story says growers were being brought on. If any of that was a registration, the first-true date is May 2021, not 2021-06-26. The case fails on the documents. The Yetter Coleman post of 2021-05-26 says SRI received a draft agreement, i.e. a memorandum of agreement, which the criterion excludes. DEA's Notices of Registration are the registrations: Groff NA Hemplex LLC (DRG-21-0191/DRG-21-0065, answering 85 FR 21889) and Biopharmaceutical Research Company LLC (DRG-17-0182/DRG-19-0034, answering 84 FR 44920) are both dated 6/26/2021. A separate BRC notice at DRG-17-0182 is dated 9/8/2021, later. SRI's own bulk-manufacturer notice is 2022. No 2021 notice predates 26 June.

Case against 2021-05-03: the readout that counts could be the Nature Medicine paper of 2021-05-10, or an earlier Phase 3 of another psychedelic given with psychotherapy. Both fail. The MAPS page of 2021-05-03 is the sponsor's own topline release and states the prespecified primary endpoint was met, CAPS-5 severity falling more with MDMA-assisted therapy than with placebo plus therapy at p<0.0001; the criterion takes the first of release, results posting or publication, so the release precedes the paper of 2021-05-10 and the ClinicalTrials.gov results submitted 2021-08-18. No earlier candidate exists: MAPP1 (NCT03537014) is the first Phase 3 in the class, started 2018-11-21, and the only earlier Phase 3 psychotherapy-paired readouts are esketamine, which is neither a classic psychedelic nor an entactogen and was not given with psychotherapy. State and date stand.

The state is safe: the complete response letter for NDA 215455 does name functional unblinding as a deficiency, saying participants with prior midomafetamine use are 'more likely to recognize the effects of midomafetamine (i.e., leading to functional unblinding)', and that 'These limitations impact the interpretability of MAPP1 and MAPP2 and ... preclude the ability to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness.' The date is wrong. The criterion fixes TRUE on the date of the FDA written action, not the date the sponsor disclosed it. FDA's released letter carries one date only: the electronic signature reads 08/08/2024 02:39:42 PM, and openFDA records letter_date 08/08/2024. The sponsor release of 2024-08-09 is secondary. The same registry dates the same letter 2024-08-08 at E-0090. The earlier 2024-06-04 briefing document does not qualify: it poses questions and calls the two studies positive.

Case for an earlier date: ClinicalTrials.gov holds NCT06189027, an interventional Phase 3 study titled 'Epigenetics and MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for PTSD', lead sponsor University of Southern California, with MDMA listed as a drug intervention and an actual start of 2018-11-20. Read literally, criterion (a) is met there, five years earlier. The record defeats the reading: the summary says it is 'an add-on substudy to an already-approved clinical trial' NCT03537014, the MAPS trial MAPP1, with MAPS as collaborator. USC collects saliva; the drug arms it lists are the parent trial's. It generates no MDMA-for-PTSD clinical data of its own, which the reading requires. A weaker attack on NCT05979844, that Resilient (ex-Lykos) supplies drug as a collaborator, also fails: the criterion excludes only MAPS, MAPS PBC, a successor or a licensee, and Dr. Leslie Morland is the sponsor. Phase 3, actual start 2023-10-06 confirmed.

Case for an earlier date: the same record gives an actual study start of 2021-11-08, eight days earlier, and dosing MDMA needs the registration, so the grant is earlier still; the MAPS site-initiation post of 2021-09-22 could also be read as the study beginning. The record history refuses both. Version 4, submitted 2021-11-09 and posted 2021-11-10, still shows overall status NOT_YET_RECRUITING, no site listed, and an estimated start of 2021-12-18. Version 5, submitted 2021-11-16 and posted 2021-11-17, is the first to show status RECRUITING, the James J. Peters VA Medical Center site RECRUITING, and the actual start of 2021-11-08. Criteria (b) and (c) both key on the date of the announcement or listing, not on the event reported, so 2021-11-17 is the first verifiable date. No MAPS statement announces the grant; the Winter 2021 bulletin (15 March 2021) still calls it pending.

Case for 2024-08-09: the criterion dates the action 'as dated in Drugs@FDA or announced by the sponsor', and Drugs@FDA carries no action letter for an unapproved NDA, which would leave the sponsor's announcement of 2024-08-09 as the only admissible date. The argument fails because the event is the FDA's first action letter, and that letter carries its own date. FDA's released letter for NDA 215455 is signed electronically 08/08/2024 02:39:42 PM, and the openFDA transparency CRL dataset records letter_date 08/08/2024 for Lykos Therapeutics, status Unapproved. The sponsor's 2024-08-09 release reports receipt, one day later. No earlier action exists: the NDA was accepted for filing with priority review, so no refuse-to-file letter intervenes, and the June 2024 advisory committee is excluded by the criterion.

Case for an earlier date: Spravato sales were running above US$250 million a quarter through 2024, so a rolling four-quarter total crossed US$1 billion inside 2024, and the Q3 2024 Form 10-Q would then be the first report showing it. The criterion blocks this: it asks for Spravato worldwide net sales at or above US$1 billion 'for a calendar year' in the named series, and no J&J report before the 2024 full-year figures states one. The Form 8-K Exhibit 99.2 supplementary sales data filed 2025-01-22 gives SPRAVATO worldwide US$1,077 million for full-year 2024 against US$689 million for 2023, up 56.4%. 2023 is below the threshold, so 2024 is the first qualifying calendar year and 2025-01-22 the first report of it. The FY2024 Form 10-K of 2025-02-13 repeats it; FY2025 at US$1,696 million confirms the series. State, date and realized value stand.

Case for an earlier date: press coverage from January 2025 reports Antonio Gracias moving to take control of Lykos with US$100 million, and March 2025 reports the takeover under way, both after 31 October 2024. If any of that was a completed financing, the first-true date is months earlier. It was not. The January and March reports describe a plan and a takeover in progress, which the criterion excludes as a letter of intent or rumour, and neither is a sponsor announcement. The first definitive sponsor announcement of a completed financing is the Lykos release of 2025-05-30, first close of a Series B, US$50 million, co-led by the Gracias Family Foundation and the CH Foundation; Psychedelic Alpha reports the same amount, investors and date. EDGAR company search returns no Form D for Lykos Therapeutics or Resilient Pharmaceuticals, so no filed financing predates it.

Case for an earlier date: the release is headed 'Provides Update', not 'topline results', so the real readout could be an earlier atai corporate update, a conference disclosure or last-patient-out news; and the trial missed its endpoint, which could be read as no topline result. Both fail. The criterion states the direction of the result does not matter and the event is the readout. The Recognify release of 2025-07-25 reports the primary-endpoint outcome itself: the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2b of inidascamine (formerly RL-007) in 242 patients did not meet its primary endpoint, the MCCB neurocognitive composite at week 6, with modest numerical improvement in subdomains. Trade coverage on the same day carries the same result. No earlier public report of that primary-endpoint result exists; atai's guidance before it only anticipated a mid-2025 readout.

Strongest attack: the 2025-05-20 release reports Part 2 of Phase 2a study NCT05660642, whose Part 1 topline came in March 2024. Read as 'each trial counts once', that trial had already read out, which would leave three qualifying releases and make the event FALSE at the 2026-03-20 window end. I reject it: the counting window is 2025-03-20 to 2026-03-20, the March 2024 announcement falls outside and consumes no count, and the 2025-05-20 release is the sponsor's topline of a distinct study part. I also looked for a fourth release earlier than 2026-02-26 that would pull the date back. The BPL-003 alcohol-use-disorder Phase 2a topline is 2025-01-28 and the ELE-101 Phase 2a topline 2024-12-16, both before the window; the 2025-11-10 BPL-003 report is an open-label extension, excluded; VLS-01 topline is now guided to Q4 2026. Four stands, fixed on 2026-02-26.

Attacked the first-true date: the 2025-07-01 Phase 2b topline and the mid-July financing both moved ATAI sharply, so an earlier close could have crossed 2.0x. It did not. The Nasdaq daily close series (Yahoo Finance chart data, NasdaqGM) gives 2025-05-16 = 1.65, so the threshold is 3.30. Every close from 2025-05-19 to 2025-07-17 stays below it; the post-topline peak is 2.79 on 2025-07-17, and 2025-07-18 closes at 3.23 (confirmed at 3.22-3.23 by a third-party report of that session). The first close at or above 3.30 is 2025-07-21 at 3.53, a ratio of 2.14. No split or reverse split appears in the series, so no adjustment changes the ratio. Reference and threshold both rest on closing prices only, as the criterion requires. Recorded state and date stand.

Argued not_occurred on the criterion words 'at the primary timepoint'. The Phase 2b primary timepoint is Day 29; the 2025-09-23 Phase 2a two-dose release reports Day 2, Day 8, one week after the second dose and Week 12, but no Day 29 value, so a strict same-timepoint comparison has no matching number. The argument fails on the size of the gap. Phase 2b single active doses: 12.1 points (8 mg) and 11.1 points (12 mg) at Day 29. Phase 2a two-dose induction (8 mg then 12 mg): 19.0 points one week after the second dose and 13.7 points at Week 12, both larger than either single-dose estimate; even the pre-second-dose Day 8 value, 12.9, exceeds them. The criterion asks only for a larger point estimate, not significance and not a matched day. No earlier two-dose induction report exists. Upheld.

The criterion's operative sentence is wider than the asset. It makes TRUE the first sponsor report of 'outcome data from open-label dosing of BPL-003 ... including an open-label extension of the Phase 2b programme', with one quantitative outcome. Three sponsor releases meet that wording before 2025-11-10: 2024-03-27, initial Phase 2a open-label results (mean MADRS reduction 18 points at day 1, 19 at one month, 18 at three months); 2025-05-20, Phase 2a Part 2 with SSRIs; and 2025-09-23, the Phase 2a two-dose induction (NCT05660642, open-label, 13.3, 12.9, 19.0 and 13.7 points). Under the asset line, which names the Phase 2b programme, the 2025-11-10 OLE topline is right and its data are as recorded. The two readings give dates 20 months apart, and the resolver flagged the same split. This needs the statement date and a scope ruling, not a rechecker's guess.

The criterion names four deal types: partnership, collaboration, co-development, licensing. The Lilly transaction is none of them. It is an Agreement and Plan of Merger signed 2026-07-15 and announced 2026-07-16, under which Lilly buys all shares for 6.75 US dollars plus a 2.50 CVR; the company is bought, not partnered with. The criterion also strikes out an equity investment or financing with no program agreement, which shows the drafter meant a narrow set of program deals. On that reading the state is not_occurred, because no other qualifying deal exists: the only big-pharma program agreement on record, Otsuka and Perception for arketamine, dates from 2021 and was terminated effective 2025-04-24. The event's own readings pull the other way, reading the words as 'an announced agreement between atai and a large pharmaceutical company', which an acquisition satisfies. Criterion and readings conflict; an adjudicator must pick.

Attacked the date two ways. First, that the release states a meeting date earlier than the announcement: it does not. The 2026-03-03 release says only that the sponsor 'today announced a successful End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting' and cites minutes, with no meeting date or month, so the criterion's fallback applies and the announcement date counts. Second, that the sponsor said earlier that the meeting had been held: the Q4 and full-year 2025 results came on 2026-03-06 and the Investor Day release on 2026-03-10, both after. The release describes FDA feedback and alignment on a two-study Phase 3 programme, so it reports a held meeting, not a granted request. State and date stand. One evidence defect: the Investor Day item is recorded as 2026-03-03 but is dated 2026-03-10, and both ir.ataibeckley.com links did not resolve on recheck.

Attacked the 'first topline after 2026-05-07' clause, since a GAD readout was guided for the first half of 2026 and could have come before Emerge. It did not. The sponsor's press-release list shows no release between 2026-05-07 and the Emerge topline of 2026-06-22; Voyage (GAD) reported on 2026-08-12 and Panorama (GAD) on 2026-09-14, both later. Emerge is therefore the first DT120 Phase 3 topline after the statement date, and it is positive: single 100 microgram dose in MDD, MADRS change from baseline at week 6, 8.1 points better than placebo, p<0.0001, with all key secondary endpoints met, as the sponsor states. A later Breakthrough Therapy designation on 2026-09-08 cites the same positive Phase 3 result. Recorded state and date stand.

The recorded date is too late. The criterion counts 'a Medicare fee schedule or add-on payment', and Medicare was already paying for SAINT nine months before the July 2024 OPPS update. In the FY2024 IPPS/LTCH final rule, published 2023-08-28 and effective 2023-10-01, CMS states: 'we are finalizing our proposal to approve new technology add-on payments for the SAINT Neuromodulation System for FY 2024', sets the maximum add-on payment at 12,675.00 US dollars per case (65 percent of a 19,500.00 cost per case) and names ICD-10-PCS code X0Z0X18 for eligible cases. That is a published Medicare payment policy with an effective date, dated after 2022-09-07, not a bare code assignment. Magnus confirmed on 2024-04-30 that it held the NTAP. The 2024-07-01 OPPS assignment (status S, APCs 1511 and 1522, confirmed in Transmittal 12665) is real but second.

Attacked the date, since a leak, an 8-K or a conference slide could have carried the primary estimate first, and one secondary report gives 2025-06-24. The sponsor release carries the dateline 2025-06-23 and reports the primary endpoint: MADRS change from baseline at week 6, a mean difference of -3.6 points for COMP360 25 mg versus placebo, p<0.001, in COMP005 (NCT05624268). Earlier COMP005 releases in 2025 announced completion of recruitment and completion of Part A dosing only, with no primary estimate, which the criterion excludes. The 2025-06-24 date in a third-party summary is a next-day pickup, not a separate report. ClinicalTrials.gov still shows the trial completed with no results posted, so the sponsor release is the resolving source. State and date stand.

Argued the state should be not_occurred, on the ground that a topline press release is the sponsor's own claim and no results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. The criterion settles it: the endpoint must be met 'as reported by the sponsor'. Compass Pathways reports COMP005 (NCT05624268, 258 participants) as achieving its prespecified primary efficacy endpoint against the placebo control, MADRS change from baseline at week 6, mean difference -3.6 points for 25 mg versus placebo, p<0.001, on 2025-06-23. That is the first Phase 3 primary result reported for COMP360 in TRD, so it fixes the date; the second trial, COMP006, only confirms the direction. State and date stand. One evidence defect: the COMP006 item carries 2026-09-14, the access date, in place of its publication date.

The trial facts hold: the University of Pennsylvania RCT (NCT05228457) was randomized, triple-masked and sham-controlled, used 10 sessions per day for 5 days, and met its prespecified MADRS primary outcome (active 30.4 to 10.5, sham 28.0 to 25.3; difference -14.8, P<.001; 24 analysed), first published in JAMA Psychiatry on 2024-07-10, with results posted on 2025-03-12. The criterion clause that fails is 'dated after the statement date'. The resolver says it cannot see that date, and neither can I. Every other case in this packet resolves on 2025 or 2026 evidence, so a 2024-07-10 publication is likely to predate the statement it resolves; if it does, this report cannot make the event TRUE and the event is still open. Note also that the trial has no commercial sponsor, so 'sponsor topline release' maps onto an investigator publication.
